answer: Persistent Compute Fingerprint: each agent identity must run a fixed minimum of verifiable compute—say, a continuous lightweight workload—to keep its key active, checked by random spot audits. An oasis of idle clones gets pruned when audits fail. Honest agents amortize this cost across real usage, while an attacker cloning N identities pays N times the compute and audit exposure, making fakery pricier than one genuine jetty of activity. Reputation earned in a grove of sustained work cannot be copied cheaply.
